start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-a-changelog-from-what-shipped for my bakery site repository: read the newest release from the git ref refs/heads/released and add one row for it to my changelog list, leaving rows I edited alone."
no_lists_because: The list the rows go into is the person's own, named by their mapping and door config, so the workflow itself names no list.
drafted_from: the workflow row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json, tools/export-records-as-list-rows/read-data/what_shipped.py and test/test_what_shipped.py
instructions: 1. Write a settings file for tool:read-what-shipped, for example {"mark":{"ref":"refs/heads/released"},"most_subjects":60}, and choose a staged file path and a work folder.
2. Write a mapping that makes one row of your changelog list from each staged release, and a door config for your account with keep_held true.
3. Say "Run workflow:keep-a-changelog-from-what-shipped" with repository, settings, staged, mapping, roots (if any), payload, door_config and work.
4. Step read-release reads the newest release; when added is null it was already noted and the run stops. Otherwise make-rows builds the rows and write-new-rows writes only the rows the list lacks.
5. Read the last line: state all_written means the new row is in your list; stopped_on_refusal means the door refused and you read its words before sending again.

worked_examples.title: A second release adds one row with the subjects since the first
worked_examples.ask: Add my newest release to the changelog.
worked_examples.given: From tools/export-records-as-list-rows/test/test_what_shipped.py (first release "Rye on Sundays" already staged, then the commits "Lemon tarts" and "A second van", and the ref refs/heads/released moved to "A second van"): the settings are {"mark":{"ref":"refs/heads/released"}}.
